item.description:

ABPZ20 KNHC 272307

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 PM PDT Mon Jul 27 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Fausto, located in the Central Pacific several hundred miles east of
the Hawaiian Islands, and on Hurricane Genevieve, located several
hundred miles southwest of the southern tip of the Baja California
Peninsula.

Tropical cyclone formation is not expected during the next 7 days.

$$
Forecaster Kelly/Evans

item.description: ...GENEVIEVE REMAINS A POWERFUL MAJOR HURRICANE... As of 8:00 PM MST Mon Jul 27 the center of Genevieve was located near 17.1, -114.6 with movement NW at 12 mph. The minimum central pressure was 939 mb with maximum sustained winds of about 145 mph.

item.title: Hurricane Genevieve Public Advisory Number 15
item.description:
Issued at 800 PM MST Mon Jul 27 2026 
963 
WTPZ32 KNHC 280235
TCPEP2
 
BULLETIN
Hurricane Genevieve Advisory Number  15
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP072026
800 PM MST Mon Jul 27 2026
 
...GENEVIEVE REMAINS A POWERFUL MAJOR HURRICANE...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 800 PM MST...0300 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...17.1N 114.6W
ABOUT 505 MI...810 KM SW OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...145 MPH...230 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NW OR 305 DEGREES AT 12 MPH...19 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...939 MB...27.73 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 800 PM MST (0300 UTC), the eye of Hurricane Genevieve was located 
near latitude 17.1 North, longitude 114.6 West. Genevieve is moving 
toward the northwest near 12 mph (19 km/h). A west-northwestward to 
northwestward motion with a decrease in forward speed is expected 
during the next couple of days.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 145 mph (230 km/h) with higher 
gusts.  Genevieve is a category 4 hurricane on the Saffir-Simpson 
Hurricane Wind Scale. Steady weakening is expected the next several 
days.

Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 45 miles (75 km) from the
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 150 miles
(240 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 939 mb (27.73 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
SURF:  Swells generated by Genevieve are affecting portions of the
southwestern coast of Mexico and the Baja California Peninsula.
These swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf and rip
current conditions. Please consult products from your local weather
office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 200 AM MST.
 
$$
Forecaster Kelly
item.author: nhcwebmaster@noaa.gov (NHC Webmaster)

item.title: Hurricane Genevieve Forecast Discussion Number 15
item.description:
Issued at 800 PM MST Mon Jul 27 2026 
199 
WTPZ42 KNHC 280236
TCDEP2
 
Hurricane Genevieve Discussion Number  15
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP072026
800 PM MST Mon Jul 27 2026
 
Genevieve continues to produce deep convection, but with a more
cloud-filled, circular eye that is cooler than it has been over the
past 24 hours. Over the last several hours, convection has been
warming and thinning along the western eyewall. There are also early
signs that an eyewall replacement cycle may be starting, marked by
two deep convective bands within the eastern portion of the inner
core. The latest objective intensity aids from UW-CIMSS range from
111 to 127 kt, while the most recent TAFB subjective CI Dvorak
estimate is T6.5/127 kt. Given recent satellite trends and these
latest estimates, the initial intensity has been set at 125 kt for
this advisory, although this may be generous.
 
The initial motion is estimated at 305/10 kt. Genevieve is currently
being steered northwestward around the western periphery of a
mid-level ridge. In 24 to 48 h, this ridge is forecast to weaken,
resulting in a slightly slower forward motion through the middle of
the forecast period. Toward the end of the foreast period, another
ridge over the eastern North Pacific is forecast to build to the
northwest of the system, allowing a faster west-northwestward motion
to resume. The latest NHC track forecast is similar to the previous
in the short term, with a slight nudge to the left in the extended,
and lies close to the HCCA corrected consensus and the Google
DeepMind ensemble mean.
 
Genevieve continues to experience fluctuations in deep convection
within the eyewall this evening, a trend that is likely to continue
over the next day or so, along with a possible eyewall replacement
cycle that could be starting now. In about two days, the environment
will become increasingly unfavorable as the system moves into a
drier, more stable mid-level airmass and over cooler SSTs along the
forecast track. Once the system crosses the 26C isotherm near 20N, a
faster rate of weakening will ensue. As a result, the NHC intensity
forecast calls for a steady weakening trend, followed by a faster
rate of weakening late this week and into the weekend. Genevieve is
expected to degenerate into a post-tropical cyclone by 120 h, as
model-simulated satellite imagery shows the system devoid of deep
convection by that time.
